findings.title: Additional close-error variant leaves an owned text-input Buffer unwiped
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Rare OS-close failure retains one bounded input allocation until reclamation; no direct disclosure, persistence or broad compromise was demonstrated. This does prevent a full CORE-conformance claim.

reproduction.fixture: A synthetic27-byte public text file, never wallet material.
reproduction.fault: Perform the real close, then inject EIO at the OS close adapter. Buffer.concat only observes its original unchanged result; no program rule is replaced.
reproduction.controls: Healthy exact-byte read succeeds and its caller wipes the result. The fault is propagated and the actual descriptor closes.
reproduction.prerequisite: An OS/host close failure after a successful bounded read. Runtime evidence uses synthetic fault injection, not a naturally failing filesystem.

findings.expected: When descriptor closure prevents a completed read from returning, the still-owned result Buffer is wiped before the failure leaves; normal success transfers live bytes to its caller.
findings.observed: readBoundedDescriptor constructs its result and wipes read chunks. readBoundedFile then executes finally closeSync; if it throws, decodedText/caller never receives the result. The actual observed result allocation retained all27 nonzero bytes after refusal.
findings.impact: Material-bearing file input can leave an additional unwiped bounded heap allocation after a rare close error. There is no output/log/network exposure in this reproduction and no guaranteed-GC or memory-recovery exploit is claimed.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the newly read Buffer owned locally until close succeeds. If close fails, wipe that unreturned result and propagate the established refusal/error contract; do not wipe a successfully transferred result before its caller can consume it.
findings.requiredVerification: Preserve this healthy control and observed red. Add a public-path regression requiring the same close failure to propagate with the abandoned result zeroed; retain normal byte-exact file/stdin reads, caller ownership and chunk cleanup on read failure.
findings.priorFindingReconciliation: Reuse the original owned-secret-cleanup family ID for this newly demonstrated additional path. The four earlier corrected paths stay verified; this is not a rollback or false claim that their accepted fixes failed.

remediation.meaning: Separate authorized post-baseline fix of the additional close-error path. The original finding remains open as a historical baseline record, not a claim about the corrected source.
